title: feat(lint): security-external-owner-unmapped warns when a writable external object refuses every member write
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"marchtian"} -->
_Requested by **田騏** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01VmuUhXU9SSUzqJYyXSmYSi?thread=cmsg_01VmuUhXU9SSUzqJYyXSmYSiVy7F2atKWpo5rp3YPrqddh)_
Fixes #27332
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` 新增一条警告 `security-external-owner-unmapped`：可写的外部对象若用按所有者的共享模型（`private`、`public_read`，或不写），又没在 `fields` 声明所有者检查读的那一列，就提示；警告点名两条出路（改 `public_read_write` 由 `beforeUpdate` hook 判谁能改；或在 `fields` 声明 `owner_id`，并让驱动以这个名字返回远端所有者——内置 SQL 驱动靠 `external.columnMap` 做到，插件驱动要自己返回，因为 `columnMap` 不由引擎执行）。
- **为什么改：** 这类对象上持有 `allowEdit` 的普通成员改任何一行、删任何一行都被 403（共享检查读 `owner_id`，所有权兜底读 `created_by == 当前用户`，远端行都没有这两列），以前 `os validate` 不提示。实测删除同样被拒；`ownership: 'none'` 不是出路（只是把拒绝从共享检查挪到兜底），所以它照样报警，改为点名 `created_by`。
- **风险与回滚：** 只是警告，不拒收，`defineStack` 和所有发布入口接受的集合不变；运行时零改动。回滚 = revert 本 PR。
- **先看：** `packages/lint/src/validate-external-owner-sharing.ts`（判定的两条分支 `undeclaredOwnershipColumn`，以及只有 `columnMap` 没声明字段时的措辞）、`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`（`os explain` 的长文）、`packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts`（登记为 advisory、仅 CLI）。
- **两分钟验证：** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run src/validate-external-owner-sharing.test.ts`，预期 14 个用例全过：spike 的 `spike_owned` 报一条警告，`spike_node`（`public_read_write`）不报，且在 `os validate` 的结果里是 advisory 不是 error。
- **需要你做的：** 无，席位落地。

## What changes

A new advisory rule, `security-external-owner-unmapped`, on all three authoring commands (`validate`, `build`, `lint`; CLI only, held off the runtime publish door for the reason every advisory object rule carries, `RUNTIME_OBJECT_ADVISORY_VOLUME`).

It warns on an object that has an `external` binding with `writable: true`, an effective sharing model that keys writes to an owner (`private`, `public_read`, or none on a custom object, which the runtime treats as `private`), and no remote column serving the check that refuses the write:

1. **Owner arm.** The object carries `owner_id` (`ownership: 'user'`, the default) as the platform's injected, unstored anchor, not declared in `fields`. Record sharing reads `owner_id`, gets null, and refuses.
2. **Floor arm.** The object carries no `owner_id` (`ownership: 'none' | 'org' | 'business_unit'`). Record sharing then abstains, and the platform ownership floor (`created_by == current_user.id`) decides. It warns when `created_by` is the unstored anchor, not declared, or when the audit columns are off (the floor then compiles to a deny).

What lets the owner write is the driver returning the remote owner under the field name the check reads. `external.columnMap` is applied by the built-in SQL drivers, not by the engine, so on a plugin driver a `columnMap` entry serves nothing. The author's vouch the rule reads is therefore a declared `owner_id` / `created_by` field (the provenance the runtime guards read: `resolveInjectedColumnProvenance`, `@objectstack/spec/data`); a `columnMap` entry alone still warns, worded for that case (works on a built-in SQL driver only). The message names the column the refusing check reads; the hint names both ways out, driver-neutrally: `public_read_write` plus a `beforeUpdate` hook, or declare the field and have the driver return the remote owner under that name (a built-in SQL driver through `external.columnMap`, a plugin driver by itself). This matches the guide wording on PR #27403 ("have your driver return the owner under the field name the checks read"). The long text (both checks, why `ownership: 'none'` is no way out, deletes) is `os explain security-external-owner-unmapped`, and agrees with the guide's "Choose the sharing model on purpose" callout (`content/docs/data-modeling/virtual-objects.mdx`, not edited here).

Supporting edits: the effective-sharing-model mirror in `validate-sharing-rule-enforceability.ts` is exported and reused instead of copied a second time; the rule id is exported from the root barrel; one changeset (`@objectstack/lint` patch).

Outside `packages/lint`: the rule count in four CLI docs transcripts (55 to 56, see notes). Not touched: the runtime, `defineStack`, the spike test (the pin lives in the lint test, with the spike's two object shapes copied verbatim), the virtual-objects guide.

### Delete (the card's third task)

Yes, the same two reads refuse `delete`. Measured over the spike's plugin-driver composition (a one-off harness, not committed): `DELETE /data/OBJECT/ID` by a member holding `allowDelete` answers 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` on the default, `private` and `public_read` models, and the remote is asked exactly `find { where: { id }, fields: ['id', 'owner_id'], limit: 1 }` then `findOne { where: { $and: [{ id }, { created_by: CALLER }] }, limit: 1 }`; `driver.delete` is never called.

One more fact the PR names because the warning's first way out depends on it: on `public_read_write` the edit passes (200) but the **delete is still refused** (403). The floor keeps deletes to `created_by` there by design (`owdOpenWritesCoversOperation` in plugin-security: that OWD opens `update` only), and an external object has no stored `created_by`. So "public_read_write plus a hook" opens member edits, not member deletes. The rule does not warn on it (the card pins `spike_node` silent); the `os explain` text says it.

### Measured: which knobs make a member edit pass

One-off boot of the spike composition (engine, sqlite default datasource, security, sharing, REST) with one external object per row on a plugin driver. Rows marked "map" ran on a variant of the driver that renames the remote column the way the SQL driver applies `columnMap` (remote column to local field), i.e. a driver that returns the owner under the checked name; the other rows' driver ignores `columnMap`, as every plugin driver does. Member holds `allowRead/allowEdit/allowDelete`; rows `r_mine` (owner or creator = member), `r_theirs` (= admin).

The SQL-driver half was measured separately on `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3) over a remote table `rows(id, name, assignee)` registered as external with `columnMap: { assignee: 'owner_id' }`: the sharing check's exact reads, `find { where: { id }, fields: ['id', 'owner_id'], limit: 1 }` and `findOne { where: { $and: [{ id }, { owner_id: U }] } }`, both return the row with `owner_id: 'u1'` (with and without `owner_id` declared); without the map the projection returns no `owner_id`.

| object shape | PATCH own | PATCH other | DELETE own | warns |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| no `sharingModel` (spike_owned) | 403 | 403 | 403 | yes (`owner_id`) |
| `private` / `public_read` | 403 | 403 | 403 | yes (`owner_id`) |
| `public_read_write` (spike_node) | 200 | 200 | 403 | no |
| `private`, map remote owner to `owner_id`, not declared | 200 | 403 | 200 | yes (columnMap wording) |
| same, plus `owner_id` declared in `fields` | 200 | 404 (read-scoped) | 200 | no |
| `private`, driver returns `owner_id` itself, declared | 200 | 404 | 200 | no |
| `private`, `ownership: 'none'` (also unset model; also `'org'`) | 403 | 403 | 403 | yes (`created_by`) |
| `private`, `ownership: 'none'`, `systemFields.audit: false` | 403 | 403 | 403 | yes (`created_by`) |
| `private`, `ownership: 'none'`, map remote creator to `created_by`, not declared | 200 | 403 | 200 | yes (columnMap wording) |
| same, plus `created_by` declared | 200 | 403 | 200 | no |
| `private`, `ownership: 'none'`, driver returns `created_by` itself, declared | 200 | 403 | 200 | no |
| same, not declared | 200 | 403 | 200 | yes (false positive, see notes) |
| `private`, `columnMap` maps only `created_by` (owner_id still injected) | 403 | 403 | 403 | yes (`owner_id`) |
| `private`, `systemFields.audit: false` | 403 | 403 | 403 | yes (`owner_id`) |

So `ownership: 'none'` is not a third way out (the neighbouring `unprovisionedAnchorFix` hint in `system-fields.ts` offers "opt the object out of the injection" for a different finding; here it only moves the refusal to the floor), and the rule keeps firing on it.

## Tests

- New `packages/lint/src/validate-external-owner-sharing.test.ts` (14 cases): the spike's two shapes through `defineStack` (`spike_owned` warns naming `owner_id` at `objects[1].sharingModel`; `spike_node` silent; through `runAuthoringRules('validate')` it lands in advisories, never errors), then the matrix above: owner-keyed models warn; `public_read_write`, `controlled_by_parent`, read-only bindings, platform-stored objects and an unset system object are silent; a declared `owner_id` silences (with or without a `columnMap` entry); a `columnMap` entry alone still warns, worded for it; a `created_by`-only map does not serve the owner check; `ownership: 'none' | 'org' | 'business_unit'` warns naming `created_by`, the audit-off variant warns, a `columnMap` entry for `created_by` alone warns, a declared `created_by` silences.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` at ee143ecb: 177 files / 7583 tests passed. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `check:test-typecheck` OK.
- Ablation (one, on the rule's silence read): the `owner === 'author'` arm removed via `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 to 0, blob 1cbc9bde to 24cd3fc6), the declared-`owner_id` case went red (1 failed / 13 passed), restore proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. (An earlier ablation on the first revision's `columnMap` silence also went red; that silence was removed when the PM's measurement showed `columnMap` is not applied by the engine.)

## Acceptance notes

- **Premise, partly corrected.** "`os validate` says nothing" is not literally true for the spike's `spike_owned`: it already gets `security-owd-unset` (error) because it declares no `sharingModel`. But that rule's hint recommends `'private'`, which on a writable external object is exactly the 403 shape; nothing named the refusal. Both now fire on `spike_owned`, and the new warning names the way out. Whether `security-owd-unset`'s hint should stop recommending `'private'` for an external object is left for the card owner; it is a wording change on a gating rule, not this card.
- **Read scoping with an undeclared owner.** In the measurement, `private` with the driver returning `owner_id` but no declared field let the member READ the admin's row (GET returned 2 of 2 remaining rows; with the field declared, 1). The sharing service's phantom-anchor test reads `fields` only, so a served-but-undeclared owner counts as unstored for reads while writes are owner-scoped. That is one more reason the rule asks for the declaration. Reported separately in the dev report; not changed here.
- **Known false positive.** A remote table whose column is literally named `created_by` (or `owner_id`) and returned by the driver, but not declared, passes the checks while the rule still warns: lint cannot see what a driver returns. The hint (declare the field) is harmless there and, for `owner_id`, also scopes reads.
- **Docs transcripts.** The new rule moves the author-time rule count `os validate` / `os build` print from 55 to 56; four CLI transcripts under `content/docs/` (`deployment/cli.mdx`, `deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`, `getting-started/build-with-claude-code.mdx`, `ui/react-pages.mdx`) are updated so `check:docs-transcript-drift` holds. Not the virtual-objects guide.
- **Guide wording.** The guide callout (PR #27403 head) and this warning agree on edits and on the driver's job. Two sentences belong to the guide's own card: deletes stay refused on `public_read_write`, and "set `sharingModel` explicitly" alone is not a way out (an explicit `'private'` is still refused); the way out is `'public_read_write'`.
- The table above came from a scratch harness that was deleted before commit; the spike's committed step (e3) remains the durable runtime pin for the edit half.
